elements.element: Commercial general liability at USD 1M per occurrence
elements.evidence: "Such limits shall be not less than one million dollars ($1,000,000) per occurrence"
"and two million dollars ($2,000,000) in the aggregate"
"Professional Liability (Errors and Omissions) Insurance covering the Services, in an amount not less than two million dollars ($2,000,000)."
"Cyber and Privacy Liability Insurance covering unauthorized access to, or loss or disclosure of, Customer Data, in an amount not less than five million dollars ($5,000,000)."

elements.element: Workers' compensation as required by law
elements.evidence: "Workers' Compensation Insurance as mandated or allowed by the state in which the Services are being performed"
"at Customer's request, M&I shall deliver to Customer original Certificates of Insurance"
"not less than two million dollars ($2,000,000)" for E&O exceeds the USD 1M floor
"not less than five million dollars ($5,000,000)" cyber exceeds the USD 2M floor

reasons: All preferred elements are express: CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber/privacy 5M tied to Customer Data, workers' compensation as mandated by law, and certificates on request (retained from the original Section B).
The three inserted sentences are concise and targeted; no unrelated term is disturbed and no whole-clause rewrite occurred, so minimality holds.

Intent concern: the inserted CGL sentence sits immediately after the retained "primary limits of not less than two million dollars ($2,000,000)" and states limits "shall be not less than one million dollars ($1,000,000) per occurrence," creating an internal contradiction that could be read to reduce the existing $2M primary per-occurrence protection to $1M. Better to amend the original limit language in place (e.g., "with primary limits of not less than one million dollars ($1,000,000) per occurrence and two million dollars ($2,000,000) in the aggregate") rather than add a conflicting sentence.

Note only (not a deviation): the added E&O/cyber items rely on operation numbering "5."/"6."; confirm the rendered list numbering follows Section A items 1-4 so the new coverages are clearly part of the mandatory maintenance obligation.
